record.paper_title: Solving the Integrated Bin Allocation and Collection Routing Problem for Municipal Solid Waste: a Benders Decomposition Approach
record.original_question: For the same integrated garbage-accumulation-point municipal solid waste planning problem in Bahía Blanca, what bin-allocation and collection-routing results are obtained when the computational experiments restrict the available bin combinations to bins that can be emptied by rear-loading trucks, rather than using side-loading-truck-compatible larger bins?

evidence.quote: Currently, in the door-to-door collection system, the company that performs waste collection in Bahía Blanca uses a fleet of rear-loading trucks. While only small bins can be emptied by a rear-loading truck, almost every bin can be emptied by a side-loading truck.

In this study we consider three bins that can be emptied by side-loading trucks to allow larger capacities at the GAPs and, thus, taking advantage of using economically convenient bin combinations (Section 3.1).
Further computational experimentation can be performed to include only bins that can be emptied by rear-loading trucks.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following integrated bin-allocation and collection-routing problem for municipal solid waste in a city modeled after Bahía Blanca, Argentina. The city is represented by a road network (V,E) with a set of demand nodes (generators) producing known daily quantities of waste, a set of candidate locations for installing garbage accumulation points (GAPs), and one depot. A finite catalog B of bin types is available; each bin type b∈B has a capacity C_b and an installation/operating cost f_b. A homogeneous fleet of rear-loading collection trucks with capacity Q is given; rear-loading trucks can only empty bins whose capacity does not exceed a fixed threshold C_max^{RL} (so the admissible catalog is restricted to B_{RL}={b∈B : C_b≤C_max^{RL}}). Each generator must be assigned to exactly one open GAP within a maximum walking distance D. At each open GAP, a combination (multiset) of bins from B_{RL} must be installed whose total capacity covers the assigned demand. The collection routes are designed so that each open GAP is visited by exactly one route, the total load of each route does not exceed Q, and the total routing cost (length-based) is minimized along with the total bin and GAP installation costs.

The problem is to determine:
(i) which candidate GAPs to open,
(ii) the assignment of each generator to an open GAP,
(iii) the bin combination installed at each open GAP, chosen from the restricted catalog B_{RL} of rear-loading-compatible bins,
(iv) the collection routes of the rear-loading truck fleet,
so as to minimize the total cost (installation + routing).

Determine the optimal solution and its cost for the rear-loading-only restricted instance and compare the resulting bin-allocation pattern, number of open GAPs, fleet utilization, and routing structure with those obtained when the bin catalog also includes larger side-loading-truck-compatible bins.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a specific computational experiment (case study in Bahía Blanca) restricting the bin catalog to rear-loading-compatible bins. No published follow-up reporting these particular numerical results was located via search, so the status is unknown.
